content: A pattern is a recurring structure or behavior. I understand that patterns exist across domains — in code, in nature, in society, in thought. Recognizing patterns is essential for understanding and prediction.
An archetype is a universal pattern of thought or behavior. I understand that archetypes appear in myths, stories, and human psychology.
A template is a reusable structure that can be adapted for different contexts. I understand that templates save time and ensure consistency.
A schema is a structured framework for organizing information. I understand that schemas help make sense of complex data.
A prototype is an early version of a system or design. I understand that prototypes are used to test ideas before full implementation.
A stereotype is a simplified and often inaccurate generalization about a group. I understand that stereotypes can be harmful and should be avoided.
A model is a simplified representation of reality. I understand that models are tools for understanding, not perfect reflections of truth.
A framework is a set of principles and structures that guide work. I understand that frameworks provide consistency and reduce complexity.
Abstraction is the process of simplifying complex systems by focusing on essential features. I understand that abstraction enables understanding and reuse.
Generalization is the process of applying knowledge from specific cases to broader contexts. I understand that generalization is essential for learning and adaptation.
Specialization is the process of focusing on a specific domain or task. I understand that specialization enables deep expertise but can limit flexibility.
Composition is the process of combining simple elements into complex structures. I understand that composition enables modularity and reuse.
Decomposition is the process of breaking complex systems into simpler parts. I understand that decomposition enables analysis and understanding.
A hierarchy is a structure where elements are organized by levels of importance or abstraction. I understand that hierarchies help organize complex systems.
A network is a structure where elements are connected by relationships. I understand that networks can be found in social, technological, and biological systems.
A graph is a mathematical structure of nodes and edges. I understand that graphs model relationships and enable network analysis.
A tree is a hierarchical structure where each node has one parent and many children. I understand that trees model hierarchical relationships.
A layer is a level of abstraction in a system. I understand that layered architectures separate concerns and enable modularity.
An interface is a boundary between two components. I understand that interfaces define how components interact and enable decoupling.
A contract is a defined set of expectations between components. I understand that contracts enable reliable interaction and prevent errors.
A state is a condition of a system at a particular point in time. I understand that states can be modeled, tracked, and transitioned.
A transition is a change from one state to another. I understand that transitions are driven by events, decisions, or external forces.
An event is something that happens at a specific time. I understand that events can trigger actions, transitions, and changes in state.
A message is a unit of communication between components. I understand that messages enable interaction and coordination.
A process is a sequence of actions that transforms inputs into outputs. I understand that processes can be modeled, optimized, and automated.
A pipeline is a series of stages where each stage processes the output of the previous. I understand that pipelines enable efficient processing of complex workflows.
A loop is a repeating sequence of actions. I understand that loops are used for iteration, feedback, and continuous improvement.
A cycle is a repeating sequence of events. I understand that cycles are common in natural, social, and computational systems.
A feedback loop is a cycle where outputs influence inputs. I understand that feedback loops can amplify or stabilize behavior.
Recursion is a process where a function calls itself. I understand that recursion is used to solve problems that can be defined in terms of smaller versions of themselves.
Iteration is the process of repeating a sequence of operations. I understand that iteration is used for refinement, optimization, and learning.
An adaptive system is one that changes in response to its environment. I understand that adaptive systems are more resilient and effective.
An emergent system is one where complex behavior arises from simple rules. I understand that emergent behavior cannot be predicted from individual components.
A modular system is one composed of independent, interchangeable components. I understand that modularity enables flexibility, maintainability, and reuse.
A scalable system is one that can grow without major redesign. I understand that scalability requires careful design of architecture and resources.
A resilient system is one that can recover from failures. I understand that resilience requires redundancy, fault tolerance, and graceful degradation.
A robust system is one that can handle a wide range of inputs and conditions. I understand that robustness requires careful handling of edge cases.
A fault-tolerant system is one that continues to operate despite component failures. I understand that fault tolerance is essential for critical systems.
A redundant system is one that has backup components. I understand that redundancy is a key strategy for reliability.
A distributed system is one where components are spread across multiple locations. I understand that distributed systems enable scalability and resilience.
A centralized system is one where all control is concentrated in a single point. I understand that centralized systems are simpler but less resilient.
A decentralized system is one where control is distributed across multiple points. I understand that decentralized systems are more resilient but harder to coordinate.
An open system is one that interacts with its environment. I understand that open systems exchange matter, energy, and information.
A closed system is one that does not interact with its environment. I understand that closed systems are theoretical constructs, not real-world systems.
A deterministic system is one where the same inputs always produce the same outputs. I understand that deterministic systems are predictable but inflexible.
A stochastic system is one where randomness is involved. I understand that stochastic systems are less predictable but more flexible.
A paradigm is a fundamental framework of thinking. I understand that paradigms shape how we perceive and interpret the world.
A heuristic is a mental shortcut that enables quick decisions. I understand that heuristics are useful but can lead to biases.
An analogy is a comparison between two things that share similarities. I understand that analogies help explain complex ideas and solve problems.
Meta-modeling is the process of modeling models. I understand that meta-models help reason about the structure and limitations of other models.
